scenario.title: Italian Spring Offensive
intro.text:
ITALIAN SPRING OFFENSIVE - 9 MAR 1941

Trebeshine Heights, Albania

In the last few weeks the Italians reinforced their army in Albania with fresh troops and we await the start of an offensive. Defend with your troops the Trebeshine Heights and if necessary recapture lost ground!

GOAL Hold after the tenth turn 10 VH, 9 VH or 8 VH for BV, V or TV!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-2-0-briliant.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.reaction-2-0-briliant.text: Klisura and its pass fell with the side roads still usable. The winter offensive has reached farther than the Italians believed a Greek army could supply.
line.reaction-2-1-victory-tactical.text: The pass is open, but some heights changed hands more than once and the supply columns learned every crater by name. We hold Klisura; spring will test whether we hold a system.
line.callback-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-0.text: The artillery officers saw Klisura open under one concentration. Now each of them finds a single decisive lock on every map. You may have taught that lesson too well.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: The men from Ballaban still trust you. They noticed that the famous pass did not receive all the guns while their road received all the wounded.
line.pindus-ridge-memory.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.pindus-ridge-memory.text: I thought the Pindus needed a reserve more than a wall. Your wall held. I have kept the reserve on this map anyway; one correct decision has not made me less cautious.
line.pindus-reserve-memory.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.pindus-reserve-memory.text: The battalion you kept back in the Pindus found the gap before headquarters did. I held one here without waiting to be told. I assumed you would ask where it was.
line.scene-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-0.text: The wire to Height 731 has been buried twice and repaired three times. The last runner brought this telephone receiver back as proof that the fourth repair is pointless.
line.scene-1.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.scene-1.text: Keep it. In a week we may need every piece of copper somewhere else.
line.scene-2.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-2.text: German columns are entering Bulgaria. There are trains for one headquarters group: west toward Kastoria, or east toward Thessaloniki. The other route will make do with what is already there.
line.decision.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.decision.text: You have held this front when holding mattered. Now tell me where your staff goes when the German attack begins.
line.decision.choice.bn4c01-choice.0.tex: Take command in Western Macedonia and cover the mountain withdrawal.
line.decision.choice.bn4c01-choice.0.hin: Route the campaign through Lake Kastoria and Metsovo Pass.
line.decision.choice.bn4c01-choice.1.tex: Take command in Central Macedonia and keep the road to Thessaloniki open.
line.decision.choice.bn4c01-choice.1.hin: Route the campaign through the retreat and evacuation at Thessaloniki.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-a-0.text: Western Macedonia leaves us farther from the fleet and closer to encirclement. I recommend Thessaloniki.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-1.text: And I recommend we stop pretending the western corps can withdraw through a mountain road without someone there to keep it open.
line.choice-a-2.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-a-2.text: Western Macedonia, then. Take the wireless truck. You will receive no second headquarters if that one is lost.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-0.text: The western battalions will hear that the port mattered more. Some of them will be right to hate us for it.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: They may. Thessaloniki keeps an army connected to its allies. We go east tonight and make that connection last longer than the frontier.
